availableCommands.name: archify
availableCommands.description: Create validated architecture, workflow, sequence, data-flow, lifecycle/state, ERD, class, tree, timeline, and waterfall diagrams as explorable standalone HTML with dark/light themes, motion and image/SVG/WebM export. Accept requirements or Mermaid; inspect repository evidence for code-backed diagrams. Use when visualizing systems, API calls, pipelines, schemas, histories, timings, or everyday steps, parts, relationships and states. Also turn an answer into a one-page explainer, with the conclusion first, structured panels, native diagrams and charts, when the user asks for a page, an explainer or an answer to share (做成一页, 用页面讲), or proactively when the user's rules opt in with an [archify explainer: ...] line. Not for dashboards.

availableCommands.name: architect
availableCommands.description: Sketch types, signatures, and module structure before code, then stay in the loop while implementation fills in. Use for /architect, 'architect this', 'design this', or non-trivial work where jumping to code would lock in the wrong shape.

availableCommands.name: arena
availableCommands.description: Spawn N parallel candidates at the same task, pick a base, graft the strongest parts of the losers into it. Use for /arena, 'arena this', 'throw it in the arena', or when one attempt at a non-trivial artifact would lock in the wrong shape.

availableCommands.name: automate-me
availableCommands.description: Use for "automate me", "create/update/refresh my -mode skill", "turn/capture my preferences or working style into a skill", or wanting agents to follow how the user works. Drafts or revises a personal -mode skill via create-skill + unslop, optionally pulling fresh evidence from recent transcripts.

availableCommands.name: axi
availableCommands.description: Agent eXperience Interface (AXI) — ergonomic standards for building CLI tools that agents use via shell execution. Use when building, modifying, or reviewing any agent-facing CLI.

availableCommands.name: benchmark-checklist
availableCommands.description: Vet a perf measurement (limiter, tuning, limits, errors, repeatability, relevance, and whether the work happened) before you report or act on it. Use when you run a benchmark or report a speedup or regression you measured.

availableCommands.name: blast-radius
availableCommands.description: Find what a change could break somewhere else before it ships, beyond the diff, and prove the one fact it's safe because of by running real code instead of writing it up. Use for 'blast radius of X', 'what could this break', or reviewing a small diff you don't trust.

availableCommands.name: bro
availableCommands.description: Restate the last message in plain human language, with no jargon.

availableCommands.name: cavecrew
availableCommands.description: When to delegate to `cavecrew-investigator` (locate code), `cavecrew-builder` (1-2 file edit) or `cavecrew-reviewer` (diff review) instead of working inline or using `Explore`. Their output is compressed, so main context lasts longer.

availableCommands.name: caveman
availableCommands.description: Terse caveman voice: answer first, fluff gone, every technical fact kept. Use for /caveman, "caveman mode", "talk like caveman", "be brief", "less tokens". Stays on until "stop caveman" or "normal mode".

availableCommands.name: chief-of-staff
availableCommands.description: Pursue a long-running goal in a single session by co-ordinating subagents.

availableCommands.name: code-review
availableCommands.description: Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along two axes: Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/spec asked for?). Runs both reviews in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to "review since X".

availableCommands.name: codebase-design
availableCommands.description: Shared vocabulary for designing deep modules. Use when the user wants to design or improve a module's interface, find deepening opportunities, decide where a seam goes, make code more testable or AI-navigable, or when another skill needs the deep-module vocabulary.

availableCommands.name: coding-guidelines
availableCommands.description: Use when asking about Rust code style or best practices. Keywords: naming, formatting, comment, clippy, rustfmt, lint, code style, best practice, P.NAM, G.FMT, code review, naming convention, variable naming, function naming, type naming, 命名规范, 代码风格, 格式化, 最佳实践, 代码审查, 怎么命名

availableCommands.name: context-mode
availableCommands.description: Keep main context clean. Delegate discovery and processing to subagents; they write artifacts to disk and return a path plus one-line conclusion. Use for research, exploration, debugging, or any multi-step task whose raw output would flood the session. Triggers - context save, context mode, delegate it out, keep my context clean.

availableCommands.name: core-actionbook
availableCommands.description: Internal support skill for actionbook MCP selectors used by Rust documentation research workflows. Use only when another rust-skills workflow explicitly requests actionbook-backed selectors.

availableCommands.name: core-agent-browser
availableCommands.description: Internal support skill for agent-browser CLI workflows used by rust-learner, docs-researcher, and crate-researcher. Use only when browser automation is explicitly required.

availableCommands.name: core-dynamic-skills
availableCommands.description: Internal command support for dynamic Rust crate skill management. Use only when explicitly invoked by /sync-crate-skills, /clean-crate-skills, or /update-crate-skill.

availableCommands.name: core-fix-skill-docs
availableCommands.description: Internal maintenance support for checking and fixing generated Rust skill documentation references. Use only when explicitly invoked by /fix-skill-docs.

availableCommands.name: correct
availableCommands.description: Find the mistakes agents keep repeating in this repo and make each one impossible. Try architecture first, then types, then a lint whose error names the fix, then a test, and write docs last. Prove each check fails on a real past mistake. Repeat this each time the operator corrects you. Use for /correct.

availableCommands.name: create-verification-skill
availableCommands.description: Generate a project-local verification skill that drives your app the way a user does — any language, framework, or platform. Use for /create-verification-skill, "make a control skill for this repo", or when a project has no scripted way to prove UI/CLI/service behavior.

availableCommands.name: skill:dag
availableCommands.description: Turn a task into a typed DAG, compile it into a strict stage queue, and run it unattended — each node proven by mechanical gates, workers interchangeable. Harness-agnostic (plain JSON spec + zero-dep `dag` CLI), so it works from any agent. Use when a request is big enough to split into dependent workstreams, when asked to "plan this as a DAG", "make stages", "dag it", or when a multi-step task needs every step proven before the next starts.

availableCommands.name: docker-agent-command-code
availableCommands.description: Run the Command Code CLI (`cmd`) as a docker-agent harness — the wiring is upstream, so use your docker-agent build or build from main if it predates it. Use when the user asks how to run command-code in docker-agent, wants an agent config with harness.type command-code, or hits `unsupported harness.type "command-code"`.

availableCommands.name: domain-cli

availableCommands.name: principle-attack-the-premise

availableCommands.description: Apply when wiring validation, error handling, or framework adapters. Concentrate guards at system boundaries (CLI, config, network, external APIs); trust internal types and keep business logic in pure functions.

availableCommands.description: Apply to any non-trivial work, not just bulk work: edits, migrations, analyses, checks. Build the tool that does it or proves it (codemod, script, generator, or a skill your subagents follow) instead of working by hand. The tool is the artifact a reviewer can rerun.

availableCommands.name: principle-encode-lessons-in-structure

availableCommands.description: Apply when facing a novel UI interaction or architectural decision with no precedent in the codebase. Build 2-3 competing prototypes and compare side by side before committing.

availableCommands.name: principle-experience-first
availableCommands.description: Apply when product, UX, or feature-scope tradeoffs come up. Choose user delight over implementation convenience; ship fewer polished features over more rough ones.

availableCommands.name: principle-explain-the-number
availableCommands.description: Apply before you trust, report, or act on a number you measured: a speedup, a regression, a throughput, a latency, or an eval result. Find what limits it, and rule out that it measured something other than the work you think.

availableCommands.name: principle-fix-root-causes
availableCommands.description: Apply when debugging. Trace each symptom back to the first place the system went wrong and fix it there. A guard is a fix only when the state it handles is legitimate.

availableCommands.name: principle-foundational-thinking
availableCommands.description: Apply before writing logic: choosing core types and data structures, sequencing scaffold-vs-feature work, asking what concurrent actors share. Get the data structures right so downstream code becomes obvious.

availableCommands.name: principle-guard-the-context-window
availableCommands.description: Apply when context is filling up: large outputs, long files, repeated reads, fan-out planning. Route bulk to subagents; keep summaries in the main thread, not raw payloads.

availableCommands.name: principle-laziness-protocol
availableCommands.description: Apply when refactoring, evaluating diff size, or tempted to add abstractions, layers, or signal threading. Bias toward deletion and the smallest change that solves the problem.

availableCommands.name: principle-make-operations-idempotent
availableCommands.description: Apply when designing commands, lifecycle steps, or processing loops that run amid crashes, restarts, and retries. Converge to the same end state regardless of partial prior runs.

availableCommands.name: principle-migrate-callers-then-delete-legacy-apis
availableCommands.description: Apply when introducing a new internal API while old callers still exist. Migrate callers and delete the old API in the same wave instead of preserving compatibility layers.

availableCommands.name: principle-minimize-reader-load

availableCommands.name: principle-model-the-domain
availableCommands.description: Apply when writing stateful logic, or when code branches a lot or repeats a shape assumption across files.

availableCommands.name: principle-never-block-on-the-human
availableCommands.description: Apply when tempted to ask 'should I do X?' on reversible work.

availableCommands.name: principle-outcome-oriented-execution
availableCommands.description: Apply during planned rewrites and migrations with explicit phase boundaries. Converge on the target architecture; don't preserve smooth intermediate states with throwaway compatibility code.

availableCommands.name: principle-prove-it-works
availableCommands.description: Apply after completing a task, before declaring done. Verify against the real artifact (run the feature, read the actual value, inspect the diff), not a proxy, self-report, or 'it compiles.'

availableCommands.name: principle-redesign-from-first-principles

availableCommands.name: principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state

availableCommands.name: principle-sequence-verifiable-units
